text:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: spike in 5xx and timeouts on /v1/generate (region: us-west). 5xx rate 6.8% over 5m, latency P95 > 3s. Graph: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/4076543210

ashwin: I got paged. seeing scheduler queue depth jumping on batcher-prod-3, backlog ~3800 reqs, avg wait ~900ms.

maria: pulling logs now. looks like a burst of long-seq requests from a handful of API keys, KV cache growth on same hosts. head-of-line blocking obvious.

ashwin: logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:02:18Z] scheduler=batcher-prod-3 queue_depth=3824 avg_wait_ms=912 max_batch_size=1024 inflight_batches=48
[2026-03-15T09:02:19Z] gateway=gw-1 status=504 route=/v1/generate err="batch deadline"
[2026-03-15T09:02:20Z] kv-cache=host-7 size_mb=743 eviction_rate=0.3
```

danny: stepping in. first mitigation: reduce max_batch_tokens and max_batch_size on the affected scheduler, and enable preemptive eviction for KV cache. doing a config push to batcher-prod-3.

maria: agreed. also throttle high-token customers at the gateway for now (soft-rate-limit 20 rps). Jordan from Support - can you quick-check which customers are affected?

support-jordan: checking now — looks like 9 customers with >5% error rates; top two are acme-ai and chatterlabs. I'll open tickets and start contacting their SREs.

ashwin: running commands:
```bash
# reduce batch size and batch token cap on the live scheduler
redwoodctl --env=prod scheduler set-config batcher-prod-3 max_batch_size=128 max_batch_tokens=256
# enable kv eviction mode: aggressive
redwoodctl --env=prod nodes set-metadata batcher-prod-3 kv_eviction=aggressive
```

incident-bot: config change applied to batcher-prod-3 (rolling, 3/3 hosts).

maria: immediate telemetry after change: queue_depth dropped from 3800 -> 600 over 40s, 5xx rate down to 2.1%, P95 falling. Good signal.

ashwin: follow-up: we should also route new requests to a smaller model variant (fast-128) for non-critical traffic to relieve the slow-model pressure. I'll create a routing rule for 10% sample.

ops-bot: routing rule created: route /v1/generate (tier:free) -> model=fast-128 fallback=standard-1w (10%).

oncall-bot: handoff reminder: ashwin -> danny for next 30m. danny is now oncall primary.

danny: taking over. next steps: continue monitoring, decide if we need to scale dedicated pool or roll a short restart of batcher-worker on host-7 to free stuck KV handles. Also adding temporary manual backpressure at the gateway for large requests.

sre-lisa: I recommend we set a hard timeout at the scheduler layer to avoid head-of-line stalls: `batch_wait_ms=500` and enable `priority-eviction=true` for requests exceeding 2k tokens. I'll prepare the change.

maria: note: origin of burst looks like a customer-side regression sending unbounded contexts. Support has been asked to throttle them. Also filing an eval to detect runaway token requests and auto-throttle in future.

support-jordan: status page draft: "We are investigating elevated error rates impacting generation requests in US-West. Partial mitigation deployed; some customers may experience reduced throughput while we stabilize."
(Will coordinate posting once Danny confirms.)

ashwin: customer impact numbers: peak requests failing ~7% of total, affected customers ~9 with priority ones experiencing 10-15% errors. No broad data loss, just timeouts and 5xx.

danny: posting to status now. I'm going to remote-restart batcher-worker on host-7 after confirming no in-flight critical batches.

maria: watch logs during restart. here's the drain command I'll run:
```bash
redwoodctl node drain host-7 --timeout 60s && systemctl restart redwood-batcher && redwoodctl node uncordon host-7
```

incident-bot: host-7 restart started at 09:03:54Z.

maria: restart complete. post-restart metrics: kv-cache back to normal, queue depth steadied ~120, 5xx ~0.9%, P95 ~680ms.

danny: good stabilization. keeping these mitigations for 1h, then slowly revert with a canary. action items:
- Ashwin: write up temporary config changes and exact timestamps (for postmortem).
- Maria: collect full logs & Grafana links, export timeline.
- Jordan: update affected customer tickets and send a customer impact summary.
- Lisa: propose automated guardrails to detect and throttle runaway long-sequence requests.

oncall-bot: reminder: post-incident handoff at 10:00Z if further followup required.

support-jordan: sent initial customer-notify emails for acme-ai + chatterlabs; both acknowledged and will adjust call patterns.

danny: I'm leaving the thread open for 30m, then will mark stable. Please ping if anything regresses. Thanks everyone for quick action. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied; degraded service reduced. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-512 for postmortem.
